solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: On paper, wage linked to performance of duty gives commendation — but not really

parts.note: the wage as it appears on paper is the slip handed over with your pay
doing one's duty, as in military or public work, is service

explanation.surface: A wage linked to performance seems to earn praise that turns out to be hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration (4,3,7) splits the combined lights differently from the grid: the first word gains an S and loses its last three letters to the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: offering praise or support in words only, without sincerity or action behind it.

clue.text: Survey area by Bolivia NW?

parts.note: Peru lies to the north-west of Bolivia, giving Peru's
the area beside Bolivia is the eastern part, E for east

explanation.surface: A surveyor studies a region near north-west Bolivia.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as Peru's E: the eastern area of Peru is the area by Bolivia's north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to look over or examine something carefully, to survey it.

clue.text: You and me repeatedly missing out on seconds — it's delicious!

indicators.note: repeatedly means the remaining letters are used twice
the second letter of each of the two words is left out

parts.note: the two words written together

explanation.surface: Two greedy eaters skip second helpings yet still declare the food delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing out on seconds' takes the O from YOU and the E from ME, leaving YUM, which 'repeatedly' doubles.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of pleasure at tasty food, said when something tastes good.

clue.text: Fall behind circle in university, having been through the mill?

indicators.note: the circle sits in the university's letters

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics
O is the shape of a circle
grain that has been through the mill is ground

explanation.surface: A student falls behind in a circle at university after a rough time.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose ground is an idiom for falling behind or losing an advantage.

clue.text: Oscar's neighbour collecting uniform in Pacific island region

indicators.note: the outer piece collects the other, holding it inside

parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet, Papa follows Oscar
Uniform is the NATO code word for U

explanation.surface: Oscar's neighbour gathers a uniform somewhere in the Pacific islands.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO alphabet O is Oscar, P Papa and U Uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Papua is the region of New Guinea, the big island in the south-western Pacific.

clue.text: See 1 across
Spinner's being this

parts.note: a spin doctor speaks for a party, and as a wheel a spinner has spokes

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a spinner really is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' is both a spin doctor and a wheel; split, the answer reads as the wheel part's man.
explanation.definitionFit: A press officer who puts a favourable spin on news speaks on behalf of an organisation.

clue.text: High status

definitions.meaning: high meat smells strong and is going off, foul-smelling
standing or position in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: High status.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul-smelling like high meat, and also one's position or grade in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Write home (home being in Home Counties?)

parts.note: to be home is to be in

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
crib is slang for one's home

explanation.surface: Write home, the brackets adding that home is in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to write or engrave words on a surface.

clue.text: Save and lend variously, subject to bond

indicators.note: done variously, the letters are taken in different ways, rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on saving and lending money, subject to a bond agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests finance; here it is the bonds of slavery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enslaved is held in bondage, subject to bonds or chains.

clue.text: Ends strange afterthought

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
PS, postscript, is the afterthought added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A strange afterthought brings things to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumps are hind ends or backsides, and also leftover remnants, so both are ends.

clue.text: Forecast for islands — westerly air coming in

indicators.note: something coming in enters the middle of the other pieces, so it is placed inside them

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: in an across clue a westerly movement runs right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A weather forecast for the islands warns of westerly winds coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westerly' reverses the tune, since in an across answer west is leftward; 'coming in' places it inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a prediction of how something, especially an illness, will turn out.

clue.text: Dissembling, grouses dreadfully over censure

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed over, covering, the other piece so that it sits within them
done dreadfully, the letters of the word are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a rap, as in a rap on the knuckles, is a reprimand

explanation.surface: Someone grouses terribly about being criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadfully' scrambles the moaning word into SOURGES, and 'over' covers the reprimand with those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending you never wanted what you could not have is the dissembling of the fox in Aesop's fable.

clue.text: You are on the phone with head of entertainment — a waste

parts.note: in phone text-speak, you are is written UR

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone on a call about entertainment dismisses it as a waste of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogen compound the body excretes in urine, a waste product.

clue.text: About time secret revolutionary socialist showed rapport with the people?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the other piece
a revolution overturns order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A secret revolutionary socialist tries to show solidarity with the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rearranges SECRET to STREEC and 'About' wraps it around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Street credibility is acceptance among ordinary, often young, urban people.

clue.text: Despicable company gets half-hearted bite after introducing lure

indicators.note: the lure is introduced into the bite, which is completed after it
the heart of the word is its doubled middle letter, and half of it goes

parts.note: a nibble is a small bite
to lure is to tempt

explanation.surface: A firm tries to hook customers with a feeble bait, which is a despicable tactic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' loses one of the two middle letters, leaving NIBLE; 'after introducing' slips the lure in just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms meaning deserving contempt or scorn.

clue.text: Schedule of action — having left out last contents of kettle, add tea, I say

indicators.note: said aloud, the drink sounds like a letter

parts.note: the drink's name sounds like the letter T

indicators.note: the left is taken out of the deposit

parts.note: the chalky deposit that remains in a kettle is limescale

explanation.surface: Kettle-cleaning instructions: empty the dregs and add tea, timed like a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' removes L (left) from LIMESCALE, and 'I say' turns tea into the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A timescale is the period over which planned events or actions are scheduled.

clue.text: Steep tumble in a dream

indicators.note: letters that tumble fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A sheer drop seen while tumbling in a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective; it is a verb, to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To marinade meat is to steep or soak it in a seasoned liquid.

clue.text: It's heat-resistant and most effective in an emergency

parts.note: an gives A

indicators.note: one piece goes in the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the emergency distress signal
the best is the most effective

explanation.surface: Something is heat-resistant and works best in an emergency, like a fire blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral formerly used for fireproofing and insulation.

clue.text: Being this, watched out? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the reverse of the order printed is used, so the second word comes first

parts.note: out means away, absent
to have minded something is to have watched over it

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful is asked if they were told to watch out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watched out' gives MINDED ABSENT; 'On the contrary' swaps the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forgetful and inattentive is in the state the clue calls 'this': distracted, with thoughts elsewhere.

clue.text: Macho, getting in a tailspin suffering from this?

indicators.note: the tail end of the word spins, its last two letters swapping places

parts.note: manful means manly, macho

explanation.surface: A tough guy goes into a spin when struck down by a mild cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting in a tailspin' swaps the last two letters of MANFUL, moving the L ahead of the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokey name for a minor cold that men are said to exaggerate, so the macho man is suffering.

clue.text: Priest presented as wit

indicators.note: the letters are presented in another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest comes across as a witty person.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is a French loanword for lively wit or spirit.

clue.text: Made cubes, topped (or not)

indicators.note: the brackets ask for the word not topped, so its first letter is lost

parts.note: to dice food is to cut it into cubes

explanation.surface: A cook chopped something into cubes and may or may not have finished it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped' serves twice: as the definition and, with '(or not)', as the signal to remove the head of DICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced can mean covered with icing, a topping, and in slang also killed, which is another sense of topped.

clue.text: Key points: 'Scuttling … silent seas'

indicators.note: scuttling things scurry about, so the letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: A literary quotation: something scuttling across the floors of silent seas, after Eliot's Prufrock.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentials are the fundamental, indispensable points of a matter.

clue.text: Number three variable

indicators.note: a variable is not fixed, so the letters can change places

explanation.surface: A maths phrase: the number three as a variable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure: read it as something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, a substance that numbs, so a numb-er.

clue.text: Fruit of regular visits to bungaloid

indicators.note: visiting at regular intervals picks every other letter

explanation.surface: A regular visitor to a sprawling bungalow estate brings fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Bungaloid is a dismissive British word for areas of sprawling bungalows.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Signer will give this pat, a rough translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A signer translating for the deaf will give a rough version of what was said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signer' suggests sign language; it is someone signing their name.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is the signature a person signs, as a celebrity does for fans.

clue.text: Direct this way or that

indicators.note: read forwards or backwards, the word gives the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An instruction to send someone this way or that.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer someone to an expert is to direct them there.

clue.text: I use net in jacuzzi here?

definitions.text: I use net in jacuzzi here?

indicators.note: letters in a jacuzzi are churned by the bubbling water

explanation.surface: Someone takes a net into the hot tub, perhaps to fish out debris.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a jacuzzi may be found in a bathroom attached to a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom adjoining a hotel bedroom is the usual place for a jacuzzi, so the question points to it.

clue.text: Perhaps express suspicion over fortress

parts.note: re means about, concerning, a sense of over as in 'fight over'
to doubt someone is one way to express suspicion of them

explanation.surface: Someone voices suspicion about a fortified position.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fort or defensive stronghold.
